sentences.text: Choyrodon barsboldi is the sole species within its genus and belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea. It is classified as a basal member of Iguanodontia, a group of ornithopod dinosaurs.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial skeleton with a skull, lower jaws, cervical ribs, and metacarpals. The skull features a supraoccipital bone overlapping on both sides, which researchers interpret as an opisthotic bone.

The genus name Choyrodon combines the Mongolian city of Choyr with the Latin word for tooth, while the species name honors the paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold. American paleontologist Terry Gates and colleagues formally named this dinosaur in 2018.
Three distinct specimens have been found in the lower member of the Khuren Dukh Formation, including the holotype MPC-D 100/801 discovered in the lower deposits of the Choeren Doe formation.

Phylogenetic analysis identifies Choyrodon as the sister taxon of Eolambia. It is distinguished from the coexisting Altirhinus by the presence of an open antorbital fenestra, a feature absent in the holotype of Altirhinus. Researchers found no evidence to support the hypothesis that Choyrodon is a juvenile form of Altirhinus.

Choyrodon lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) in the Khuren Dukh Formation of Mongolia, approximately 110 to 100 million years ago. The fossil record for this animal spans from 110.1 to 100.5 million years ago in what is now Asia.
While some suggest Choyrodon is merely a juvenile Altirhinus, the describers argue against this based on specific anatomical differences.
